extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of GAP (computational algebra system); mathematicians and programmers implementing algebraic computations
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual guidance and behavioral specifications for GAP operations on polynomial rings, monomial orderings, Groebner bases, rational functions, algebraic and p-adic extensions. Includes API semantics, representation constraints, performance notes, and warnings for NC (no-check) variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial ordering properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A monomial ordering is total, invariant under multiplication with other monomials, and admits no infinite descending chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering should normally be admissible (compatible with products): if a < b then ca < cb for all monomials a, b, c. See [CLO97] for details. Monomial orderings are represented by objects providing comparison functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MonomialComparisonFunction / MonomialExtrepComparisonFun
rubrics_metrics.description: Each monomial ordering object provides MonomialComparisonFunction and MonomialExtrepComparisonFun to compare monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions work as 'is less than' (return true iff left argument is smaller). MonomialComparisonFunction compares monomials/polynomials; MonomialExtrepComparisonFun compares monomials in external (list) representation and is used internally for algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: MonomialLexOrdering semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexicographic ordering: monomials compared first by exponents of largest variable, then by second largest, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variables are ordered by internal index (x1 > x2 > ...). Optional vari argument (list of variables or indices) specifies a custom descending variable order.

rubrics_metrics.name: MonomialGrlexOrdering semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree/lexicographic ordering: monomials compared first by total degree, then lexicographically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variables ordered by internal index by default; optional vari list can specify variable order.

rubrics_metrics.name: MonomialGrevlexOrdering semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Grevlex ordering: monomials compared first by total degree, then by backwards lexicographic order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differs from grlex with variables reversed. Variables ordered by internal index by default; vari can override.

rubrics_metrics.name: EliminationOrdering semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Elimination ordering: compares monomials first by exponent vectors for variables in elim (lexicographically w.r.t. elim order), then compares the remaining variables by a graded lexicographic ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both elim and rest may be lists of variables or variable indices. Use when eliminating specified variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeadingMonomial/LeadingTerm/LeadingCoefficient behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: LeadingMonomialOfPolynomial(pol, ord) returns the leading monomial of pol with respect to ord. LeadingTermOfPolynomial returns the product of leading coefficient and leading monomial. LeadingCoefficientOfPolynomial returns the leading coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions depend on the chosen monomial ordering; examples show different leaders under lex vs grlex orderings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PolynomialReduction semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: PolynomialReduction(poly, gens, order) reduces poly by the ideal generated by gens using monomial order order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless gens is a Groebner basis the result is not guaranteed to be unique. Returns [remainder, list_of_quotients]. Strategy differs from the textbook division algorithm (see PolynomialDivisionAlgorithm).

rubrics_metrics.name: PolynomialReducedRemainder behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: PolynomialReducedRemainder(poly, gens, order) behaves like PolynomialReduction but returns only the remainder (faster because it doesn't keep quotients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when only remainder is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PolynomialDivisionAlgorithm semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Implements the division algorithm for multivariate polynomials as in [CLO97, Theorem 3 in Chapter 2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be slower than PolynomialReduction but the remainders are guaranteed to agree with the textbook algorithm. Returns [remainder, list_of_quotients].

rubrics_metrics.name: Groebner basis definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A Groebner basis G of an ideal I (w.r.t. a monomial ordering) is a set of generators such that the ideal generated by the leading monomials of G equals the ideal generated by the leading monomials of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See [CLO97] for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: GroebnerBasis operation behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: GroebnerBasis(L, O) or GroebnerBasis(I, O) returns a Groebner basis of the ideal generated by L or I with respect to ordering O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP's current implementation is a naïve Buchberger algorithm intended mainly as a teaching tool and might not be sufficient for serious problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: GroebnerBasisNC behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: GroebnerBasisNC(L, O) works like GroebnerBasis but the first argument must be a list and no test is performed to check whether the ordering is defined for all occurring variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for speed when inputs are known valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Groebner basis definition and computation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Groebner basis B is reduced if no monomial in a polynomial in B is divisible by the leading monomial of another polynomial in B. ReducedGroebnerBasis computes a Groebner basis and then reduces it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ReducedGroebnerBasis(L, O) returns a reduced basis for ordering O; examples show different reduced bases under different orderings.

rubrics_metrics.name: StoredGroebnerBasis attribute usage
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ideal I, StoredGroebnerBasis(I) holds a list [B, O] where B is a Groebner basis for monomial ordering O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be used to test membership or obtain canonical coset representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: InfoGroebner purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: InfoGroebner is an info class that gives information about Groebner basis calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to obtain informational/debugging output during Groebner computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse monomial orderings for performance
rubrics_metrics.description: For performance reasons it can be advantageous to define monomial orderings once and then reuse them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ord := MonomialGrlexOrdering(); then pass ord to GroebnerBasis/ReducedGroebnerBasis to avoid recomputing ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational function representations
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP uses four representations for rational functions: numerator/denominator, polynomials, univariate rational functions (coefficient lists + valuation), and Laurent polynomials (coeff list + valuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representations do not necessarily reflect mathematical properties; conversion and attributes allow treating objects conceptually regardless of internal representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining attributes as conceptual representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each representation is associated with one or several 'defining attributes' that give an external representation (lists) and are the defining information telling a rational function what it is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods for rational functions are installed for properties and not for representations; functions should use these attributes rather than relying on internal representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: External representation format for monomials and polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: A monomial is stored as an expanded list [inum, exp, inum, exp,...] sorted by indeterminate numbers. A polynomial is stored as [mon, coeff, mon, coeff,...] where monomials must be sorted according to the total degree/lexicographic order (grlex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering chosen so that addition of polynomials becomes linear in number of monomials (not quadratic) and is compatible with multiplication, improving quotient calculation performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRationalFunctionDefaultRep / IsPolynomialDefaultRep semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRationalFunctionDefaultRep and IsPolynomialDefaultRep designate default internal representations; these representations are defined by attributes such as ExtRepNumeratorRatFun, ExtRepDenominatorRatFun, and ExtRepPolynomialRatFun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes return external representations (lists) used as conceptual views of the object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions should use attribute-level interfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms should use attributes like ExtRepDenominatorRatFun, CoefficientsOfLaurentPolynomial, IndeterminateNumberOfUnivariateRationalFunction as the low-level interface to work with polynomials rather than referring to actual representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures algorithms work irrespective of internal representation and avoids expensive conversions unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation functions NC variants warning
rubrics_metrics.description: NC variants (e.g., RationalFunctionByExtRepNC, PolynomialByExtRepNC, LaurentPolynomialByExtRepNC, AlgebraicExtensionNC) do not perform tests of arguments and can create illegal/invalid objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NC variants only if speed is required and the arguments are known to be in correct form.

rubrics_metrics.name: RationalFunctionByExtRep behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: RationalFunctionByExtRep(rfam, num, den) constructs a rational function in family rfam from external representations num and den; no cancellation takes place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When cancellation is desired, use RationalFunctionByExtRepWithCancellation which will attempt cancellation (not necessarily optimal).

rubrics_metrics.name: PolynomialByExtRep and LaurentPolynomialByExtRep behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: PolynomialByExtRep constructs a polynomial from an external representation; LaurentPolynomialByExtRep constructs a Laurent polynomial from coefficients and valuation with no coefficient shifting performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer higher-level constructors (e.g., LaurentPolynomialByCoefficients) unless parameters are guaranteed correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: ZippedSum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ZippedSum(z1, z2, czero, funcs) computes the sum of two external polynomial representations. funcs is [monomial_less, coefficient_sum].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: coefficient_sum must be a proper summation function (not a difference). The component fam!.zippedSum holds this list for the family.

rubrics_metrics.name: ZippedProduct requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ZippedProduct(z1, z2, czero, funcs) computes the product of two external polynomial representations. funcs is [monomial_prod, monomial_less, coefficient_sum, coefficient_prod].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions are found in the component fam!.zippedProduct of the rational functions family.

rubrics_metrics.name: QuotientPolynomialsExtRep behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: QuotientPolynomialsExtRep(fam, a, b) computes the external representation of the quotient of polynomials represented by a and b, returning fail if b does not divide a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test exact divisibility at external representation level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation heuristics and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: TryGcdCancelExtRepPolynomials attempts to cancel common factors between two external polynomial representations; HeuristicCancelPolynomialsExtRep performs the actual heuristic cancellation and may return fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because there is no proper multivariate GCD, cancellation is not guaranteed to be optimal; RationalFunctionByExtRepWithCancellation uses these functions to try to reduce numerator/denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: PolynomialRing / IsPolynomialRing categories
rubrics_metrics.description: PolynomialRing(R, n) and variants create polynomial rings; IsPolynomialRing(pring) is the category test. Specialized category tests exist such as IsFiniteFieldPolynomialRing, IsRationalsPolynomialRing, IsUnivariatePolynomialRing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to create rings with named indeterminates, with avoid lists, or from existing indeterminates. Category tests indicate the base ring type and arity.

rubrics_metrics.name: FunctionField creation variants and avoid semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: FunctionField(R, rank[, avoid]) or FunctionField(R, names[, avoid]) or FunctionField(R, indets) create function fields over integral ring R in specified indeterminates. avoid is a list of indeterminates whose internal index numbers should be skipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indeterminates created independently may differ though they might display identically; use IndeterminatesOfFunctionField to get indeterminates. The avoid argument ensures newly created indeterminate indices do not clash with existing ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnivariatePolynomialRing avoid and naming semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: UnivariatePolynomialRing(R[, nr]) or UnivariatePolynomialRing(R[, name][, avoid]) returns a univariate polynomial ring in indeterminate nr (default 1). If an avoid list is given, the chosen indeterminate will differ from those in avoid. A string name can be prescribed for the indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use avoid to guarantee distinct indeterminates across constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groebner basis teaching-tool warning
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP's Buchberger implementation is mainly intended as a teaching tool and may not be sufficient for serious problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For heavy-duty Groebner computations consider external specialized software; in GAP reuse orderings and be aware of performance limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: AlgebraicExtension creation semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: AlgebraicExtension(K, f[, nam]) constructs an extension L of field K by one root of irreducible polynomial f; by default the root is printed as 'a' unless nam provided. AlgebraicExtensionNC skips irreducibility check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: L.LeftActingDomain is K; DefiningPolynomial and RootOfDefiningPolynomial attributes hold f and a root respectively. Use NC variant only when inputs are validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic extension element representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of an algebraic extension are considered polynomials in the primitive element; external representations are the polynomial coefficients in the primitive element a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base field elements are displayed with a leading exclamation mark to indicate they are different from elements of the extension. Lists mixing base-field and extension elements are not homogeneous; multiply with One(extension) to embed base-field entries in the extension before using as polynomial coefficients or matrix entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: IdealDecompositionsOfPolynomial purpose and output
rubrics_metrics.description: IdealDecompositionsOfPolynomial(pol) finds pairs g,h with deg(g), deg(h) < deg(f) such that f(x) | g(h(x)), corresponding to proper subfields of an algebraic extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns list of pairs [g,h]; option onlyone returns at most one decomposition (faster). Used to determine subfields of a given algebraic extension; example demonstrates usage with Galois group Q8.

rubrics_metrics.name: p-adic number family precision semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: PurePadicNumberFamily(p, precision) returns the family of pure p-adic numbers over prime p with given precision digits; approximate values differ from correct value by a multiple of p^digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PadicNumber(fam, rat) returns the element of the p-adic family approximating the rational rat. Arithmetic is performed with the family precision; p-adic approximations are ring homomorphisms on certain subrings so rounding errors do not grow with repeated calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PadicExtensionNumberFamily construction constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: PadicExtensionNumberFamily(p, precision, unram, ram) constructs an extended p-adic field L isomorphic to Qp[x,y]/(h(x), g(y)) where unram are coefficients of a cyclotomic polynomial (unramified part) and ram are coefficients of an Eisenstein polynomial or 1+x (ramified part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP does not check that unram corresponds to a cyclotomic polynomial or that ram is Eisenstein; the user must ensure these correctness conditions.
